subject: Take-home assignment and timeline — Backend Engineer (Casey Jordan)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
To: Casey Jordan <casey.jordan@example.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Take-home assignment and timeline — Backend Engineer (Casey Jordan)

Hi Casey,

Thanks again for your time in the interviews last week — it was great to meet you. As discussed, please find attached a short take-home assignment that mirrors a typical problem our backend team works on. The goal is not to write a full production system but to show your approach to design, trade-offs, and a working prototype.

Timeline:
- Assignment sent: today (Feb 10)
- Deadline: Tue, Feb 17 by 5:00 PM PT
- Submission: email back to me (laura_bennett@redwoodai.com) with the subject line: "Take-home submission — Casey Jordan"

Guidelines (short):
- Timebox: ~8 hours recommended
- You can use standard Python libraries and the web framework of your choice (Flask/FastAPI). Please avoid heavy external services or paid APIs.
- Include a README that explains how to run your demo and any trade-offs you considered.
- We'll ask two interviewers to review and we'll schedule a 45-minute debrief afterward.

Rubric and scoring details are here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rHk-example-rubric

Attachment: takehome-backend.pdf (prompt + sample data)

If you have any clarifying questions while you work on this, feel free to reply — we won't penalize clarifying Qs.

Good luck,

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Engineering Manager, Backend
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodai.com

From: Casey Jordan <casey.jordan@example.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Take-home assignment and timeline — Backend Engineer (Casey Jordan)

Hi Laura — thanks for sending this over and for the clear rubric. A couple quick questions before I start: 

1) Are we allowed to use SQLAlchemy (ORM) for the small persistence piece, or should it be raw SQL?
2) For the sample dataset, is it okay to mock an in-memory store instead of spinning up Postgres?

I want to make sure I focus on the items you care about.

Thanks,
Casey

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodai.com>
To: Casey Jordan <casey.jordan@example.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Take-home assignment and timeline — Backend Engineer (Casey Jordan)

Hi Casey — quick reply from the recruiting side and copying Laura for completeness.

1) SQLAlchemy is fine — we don't expect perfect database modeling for this exercise, just a reasonable approach.
2) An in-memory mock or SQLite is totally acceptable for the submission. If you note the substitution in the README, that's sufficient.

If you want, Laura can add any role-specific preferences but otherwise you're good to proceed.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Talent Partner
priyom_das@redwoodai.com
